answer: Each identity must complete a challenge-specific chain of sequential modular squarings before its Wesolowski proof is accepted; each step depends on the previous one, so GPUs cannot parallelize that chain to shorten its elapsed time. Clones may run separate chains concurrently, but each still incurs the same time bottleneck, limiting rapid identity creation. A saffron-tagged request or basalt hardware does not bypass the delay; even a comet-fast device must perform the sequential work.
